Enable scalable and modular execution of complex robotic behaviors - Ensure that robotics systems meet strict latency and reliability requirements - Optimize for resource-constrained and embedded environments - Develop tools to monitor system health, debug failures, and analyze performance - Design and maintain deployment workflows, CI/CD pipelines, and containerization (e.g., Docker) - Build abstractions, APIs, and tools that enable application engineers to develop robotic behaviors efficiently - Experience working with real-time constraints and performance-critical systems - Strong proficiency in Python programming - Familiarity with robotics middleware frameworks (e.g., DDS, Zenoh, ROS2) - Experience with containerization, CI/CD, and codebase management at scale - Ability to design clean abstractions and APIs for internal users - Experience building tools or interfaces for operators or engineers NICE TO HAVE - Background in building operator tools or robotics UIs - Experience supporting ML-driven robotic systems

baincapitalventures-hera:ashbyhq:0c32686.description: THE PROBLEM HERA IS SOLVING Every complex system in America has a profession whose job it is to be your trusted guide. The legal system has lawyers. Taxes have accountants. Healthcare, a trillion-dollar industry that touches every family, leaves us on our own. 99% of care happens when someone steps outside the four walls of a doctor's office. Hera is creating a new profession to fill that last-mile gap: the Hero, a dedicated senior care expert for your family. Our Heroes educate, coordinate, and advocate for the most vulnerable population in the country. We're covered by insurance, so we can serve every family in America. The bottleneck isn't demand, it's supply. There aren't enough experts to serve every family who needs us. To scale, we need to unbundle expertise from any one human and broaden the aperture of who can become a Hero. We're building a platform that turns anyone capable of fostering human connection into a world-class care expert and upholds our brand promise at every touchpoint. Healthcare navigation today runs on tribal knowledge. One social worker knows the trick to expediting Medicaid in New York. Another knows which home-visiting physical therapist families actually love. Our platform captures every interaction, every solved problem, every hard-won insight from our expert Heroes in the field — and turns it into compounding intelligence that makes every user on the platform smarter. Think Waymo's approach to autonomy: high-quality human experts do the driving today, and every mile they log trains the system.. WHY DESIGN MATTERS MORE HERE THAN ANYWHERE ELSE We're in the business of trust. We're designing for the most emotionally charged moments of our customers' lives. Hera's brand promise is simple: care that would only be great enough for our own parents. That promise is our moat. It's what physicians refer to, what families buy, what Heroes deliver, and what the product must unlock and enforce at every touchpoint. We serve two audiences that most tech startups never build for: social workers and nurses on one side, aging parents and their adult children on the other. Trust is built or broken in every interaction, and the product is where that trust lives. WHAT WE BELIEVE IN DESIGN AT HERA We want Hera to have a soul. That means every touchpoint with Hera, the brand, the product, the first phone call, should make you feel taken care of. The product should be incredibly intuitive (that your grandma can figure it out) and opinionated; it’s not giving you all the bells and whistles but holding your hand on the best way to use it. The products I love, Granola, Arc, Linear, have a soul and just work magically in the background. Someone was in the room making decisions about what mattered and what didn't. It's the opposite of the AI slop flooding the world right now. Healthcare is the worst offender. Clinicians can be incredible, but the systems and software around them are built without trust or care — and families feel it. We obsess over the details because that's where trust gets built. I care, maybe too much, where I’ll give feedback on copy that’s already fine and I’ll send you a slack at midnight about a font weight. If that sounds annoying, we probably won’t work well together but if it sounds invigorating to give a damn, come build with us. ABOUT THE ROLE You'd be the founding product designer at Hera. You'll own three surfaces: - The Hero platform — the AI teammate that is guiding our Heroes in doing their job ensuring expert-level care at every interaction - The family experience — how aging parents and their adult children find us, trust us, and stay with us through the hardest experience of their lives - The brand that binds them — the visual and interaction language that signals, in the first thirty seconds, that Hera is human and soulful You'll report to Jenny (CEO) and partner daily with Myles (CTO), building alongside our founding engineers and Heroes in the field. bakarlabs-arcadia-science:lever:9af2728c.description: We are Arcadia Science, an evolutionary biology company founded and led by scientists. Our mission is to turn natural innovations into real-world solutions by developing systematic and quantitative approaches to leveraging biology for therapeutics R&D. We share our research as openly as possible to accelerate discovery and make our work broadly useful. We're closing the gap between biological data and biological understanding. Our Validation team does this by closing the design–build–test–learn loop through lab validation across diverse organisms. Read more about our work through our publications. We are seeking a Quantitative Biologist to join our Validation team with strong expertise in using computational analyses across modalities and biological scales to extract meaning from complex data, identifying the limits of existing analytical approaches, and developing new ones to address them. In this role, you will work shoulder-to-shoulder with experimental biologists, and bring your own firsthand experience at the bench to inform how data is collected, analyzed, and interpreted. You’ll work with imaging modalities (Raman spectroscopy, coherent Raman imaging, live-cell microscopy, quantitative phase imaging) and a range of other quantitative measurements across diverse organisms. Your contributions will be instrumental in validating existing tools at Arcadia, shaping how we design and interpret experiments, identifying potential assets, and building robust analytical infrastructure that scales across the team. Top candidates are rigorous, collaborative scientists who are equally at home writing computational pipelines and sitting down with a wet-lab colleague to think through a statistical analysis. They have strong intuitions about image data, high expectations for rigorous experimental design, and the communication skills to make quantitative reasoning accessible to scientists with diverse backgrounds. They have hands-on bench experience, generating biological data themselves and understanding the experimental realities that shape what analysis is even possible. Enthusiasm and independent documentation for participation in open science is also required as we routinely share our findings via our open-source pubs. sequoia-meter:ashbyhq:f71471f3-da51-405d.description: Meter’s ambition is to evolve internet infrastructure into a utility by building a product that caters to stakeholders from Customers, ISPs, Partners, and Technicians. Every utility starts with an installation – and that’s where you come in. The Technician Operations team is the live backbone of Meter’s deployment engine, ensuring that we deliver critical infrastructure on time, to standard, and with zero friction for our partners and customers. A Network is most vulnerable during deployment - and each stakeholder plays an essential role to ensure it’s built as performance and resilient critical infrastructure. Meter dedicates a team to each stakeholder, ensuring our product and work empowers stakeholders to do operationally and technically sound work at scale. In this role, you’ll build Meter for technicians. By guiding field technicians in real time, troubleshooting issues as they happen, and building the systems and tools that make installations effortless, you’ll ensure our product works where it matters most: in the field. WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE Your fingerprints will be on every installation, shaping the technician experience and driving the scale Meter needs to reach utility status. In your first six months, you will: - Keep projects on track: Deliver >90% of installations on time by owning live technician support and unblocking issues in real time. - Raise quality standards: Reduce rework rates <5% and ensure compliance with installation artifacts and validation checks. - Accelerate installs: Partner with Operations Engineering to roll out automated technician tooling that cuts install validation times by 30%. WHAT YOUR DAY-TO-DAY WILL LOOK LIKE From day one, you’ll be in the center of the action. A typical week might include: - Acting as the technical lead on the live install thread: Running pre-install prep calls with technicians, deciding what gets resolved on the call vs. escalated to Wired or Wireless Deployment Engineering, and owning the shift handoff so context never drops. - Real-time troubleshooting of issues mid-install: ISP circuit turn-up, native VLAN mismatches, trunk vs. access port config on AP uplinks, DHCP reservations and inter-VLAN routing, IPSec tunnel failures, HA firewall failover, DAC cable issues on backup uplinks, and more. - Owning sign-off as the final gate before a network goes live: clearing the Dashboard Issues page, confirming all hardware (firewalls, switches, APs, PDUs) is online and on the current NOS, validating ISP quality and HA failover, executing VLAN auto-config, and signing off in the deployment thread. No network activates without you. - Keeping installs moving: Documenting progress across active deployments, pushing updates to technical project managers and stakeholders, and proactively surfacing blockers before they slip. - Closing the feedback loop: Identifying recurring failure patterns and partnering with Operations Engineering to ship new playbooks, tooling, or product fixes. - Building for the field: Translating technician insights into hardware and software improvements so our product is purpose-built for how installs actually happen. Your work will directly define how Meter scales installation quality and speed worldwide. WHO YOU ARE You thrive on solving problems in real time and making order out of chaos. skydeck-superannotate:lever:e66852a8-740.description: About SuperAnnotate SuperAnnotate helps the world’s leading AI teams build responsible, next-generation models powered by high-quality human data. We’re a fast-growing Series B startup bridging the gap between advanced AI innovation and the data that drives it. Our global network of expert specialists, scalable managed operations, precise talent matching, and full project transparency ensure unmatched data quality at scale. Trusted by innovators like Databricks and ServiceNow - and backed by NVIDIA, Dell Technologies Capital, Databricks Ventures, Cox Enterprises, and Lionel Messi’s Play Time VC - SuperAnnotate is proud to be the top-ranked AI data company on G2 for multiple consecutive years, including 2025. The Impact You'll Make We’re looking for a skilled operator who can take full ownership of our most complex, high-value client engagements. As a Strategic Projects Lead, you’ll run the end-to-end delivery of SuperAnnotate’s largest LLM and Gen AI data programs. This includes everything from scoping data collection workflows with key clients, acting as a trusted resource to researchers, resolving a quality issue, reallocating resources under a tight deadline, and more. The role touches everything: strategy, execution, client relationships, team development, and process design. You’ll work directly with researchers, data teams, and other key stakeholders at some of the most advanced AI organizations in the world. You’ll be trusted to represent SuperAnnotate at the highest level - and to grow those relationships through execution and management excellence. You don't need to be building models — but you do need to be technical enough to understand how they're trained, evaluated, and improved. That means hands-on comfort with data, code, and pipelines, and the ability to engage credibly with client engineering and research teams on LLM data challenges and evaluation approaches. This is a full-time, hybrid position based in San Francisco.
